summary: Core renderer swap lifecycle, callback leases, and effect microtask ordering pass independent review and the focused runtime suite passes 23/23. Amend for two protocol gaps: restoreFocus returning undefined is recorded as success, and a rejected Promise returned from a renderer method becomes an unhandled rejection after the runtime correctly fails closed.

independent_failure_probe.result: restoreFocus(undefined) committed and diagnostics reported focusRestored=true; nextRenderer.update() returning Promise.reject caused RuntimeFailure(stage=renderer-replacement) and a separate unhandledRejection event.

findings.summary: Any non-false restoreFocus return is reported as restored; undefined currently commits successfully. Validate the hook result and focusState record shape.

Rejecting a returned native Promise throws the intended synchronous RuntimeFailure but leaves its rejection unhandled on the next turn. Observe/suppress the rejected renderer promise while preserving fail-closed swap behavior.

passed_invariants: Successful swap uses the cached Go View and appends no application tick or dispatch ID; authored tests compare Init/Update/View call counts and trace history.
A valid completion injected during replacement is accepted and immediately duplicate-fenced, remains pending in the synchronous return snapshot, and commits once in a microtask after return.
Unmount before held completion drain cancels it without an application Update or resurrection.
Retired renderer callbacks are recorded out-of-band; a callback from the active renderer after runtime unmount records the existing suppressed attempted-action tick.
Declared async renderer methods reject before teardown; a returned thenable after teardown produces RuntimeFailure and renderer-unavailable snapshot behavior without rollback claims.

limits: The two findings concern malformed renderer protocol returns; the shipped React and DOM renderers return boolean focus results and synchronous updates.
Full React-to-DOM browser integration and physical focus transfer remain pending N3; this review does not claim that gate passed.
